internal_discovery.plain_explanation: Every one of the 3 confirmed occurrences is the exact same word — الْمَشْـَٔمَة (al-mash'amah, maf'alah pattern) — in the exact same genitive phrase أَصْحَٰبُ الْمَشْـَٔمَةِ "the companions of the left/ill-omen." In 56:9 it appears twice (the emphatic doubling أصحاب المشأمة ما أصحاب المشأمة), and in 90:19 it labels those who disbelieved in God's signs. Across all three the word designates the doomed group placed on the ill-fated left side at the reckoning, in explicit or implicit contrast with أصحاب الميمنة ("the companions of the right", from the antonym root ي م ن). The root's contribution — the left as the ominous, damnation-marked direction — is present in every occurrence. However, because the evidence is a single word-type in a single construction repeated three times, the contribution cannot be tested across formal or contextual variation.
internal_discovery.layer_separation_note: FORM: all 3 are pattern N, the maf'alah noun al-mash'amah (an abstractive/locative noun of the left side). CONSTRUCTION: all 3 are the second term of an iḍāfah headed by أصحاب ("companions/people of ___"). PARTICIPANTS: the referent group is the disbelievers/damned (explicit in 90:19: الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا بِآيَاتِنَا). CONTEXT: eschatological sorting of humanity into cohorts (Sūrat al-Wāqiʿah's tripartite split; Sūrat al-Balad's two-way split). After subtracting form (maf'alah noun), the fixed collocation (أصحاب + genitive), and the Judgment-Day context, the ROOT residue is: "the LEFT side as the inauspicious/ill-fated direction."
internal_discovery.strongest_counterexample: There is no dissenting occurrence — but the strongest challenge is structural rather than a counterexample: all 3 tokens are one and the same lexeme (المشأمة) in one and the same construction (أصحاب المشأمة). Universal presence is therefore satisfied trivially, because there is only one word-type to satisfy it. No occurrence exercises a different form, a different collocation, or a non-eschatological sense, so the residue is never stress-tested. The nearest thing to a tension is 90:19, where the ill-omen coloring is discharged entirely by the surrounding كَفَرُوا clause, leaving open whether المشأمة itself contributes "ill-omen" or merely "left/the-left-group" with omen supplied contextually.
internal_discovery.competing_hypothesis: The observed meaning may reside in a LEXICALIZED technical term المشأمة ("the [people of the] left = the damned") rather than in a live, decomposable root residue. On this reading the eschatological/ill-omen sense is a frozen property of the fixed noun-collocation أصحاب المشأمة, not a productive contribution of ش-أ-م recoverable across contexts. With N=1 word-type, the packet cannot discriminate "root contributes 'ominous-left'" from "the word المشأمة lexically means 'the damned cohort'." A secondary competing hypothesis: the core root sense is bare directional "left" (as in some usages of the root), with "ill-omen" being a contextual entailment of the left = losing/doomed side at Judgment, not part of the root residue itself.
internal_discovery.distinctiveness_note: The residue is distinctive against its nearest neighbor ي م ن (yamana → الميمنة, "the right/blessed side"), which is its direct antonym and co-occurs in the same passage (56:8 أصحاب الميمنة vs 56:9 أصحاب المشأمة). It is also distinguishable from the plain directional-left roots ي س ر / ش م ل (yasār / shimāl), which denote "left" without the fatalistic/ominous coloring that ش-أ-م adds. So the residue is non-empty and directionally contrastive. Its falsifiability, however, is weak here: with no varied occurrences in the packet, the claim "left-as-ill-omen (not mere left)" cannot be independently confirmed or refuted from the evidence alone.
internal_discovery.rationale: Universal presence formally HOLDS: the candidate contribution — the left side as the inauspicious/ill-fated direction — is demonstrably present in all 3/3 confirmed occurrences, with zero resistant tokens, so the result is PREFERRED rather than UNRESOLVED. Strength is WEAK because the evidentiary base is minimal and non-diverse: a single word-type (المشأمة) in a single construction (أصحاب المشأمة) repeated three times, two of which are the same verse (56:9). Such data satisfies universal presence trivially and cannot separate a live ROOT residue from a lexicalized noun meaning (see competing hypothesis), nor stress-test the "ill-omen vs. bare-left" distinction. The residue is non-empty and distinctive against ي م ن / ي س ر, but its falsifiability is not exercised by the packet. Honest verdict: a consistent, plausible contribution that holds across full coverage, held at low confidence due to thin, homogeneous evidence.

adversarial_verification.notes: All 3 confirmed occurrences (56:9 twice, 90:19) are the identical lexeme al-mash'amah in the identical construction ashab al-mash'amah, naming the damned cohort by the LEFT side. In both surahs it stands in explicit antithesis to ashab al-maymanah (56:8; 90:18, the blessed right), so the directional 'left(-hand side)' + inauspicious/ill-omened coloring co-occur in every case; the root sh-'-m lexically fuses left-side and ill-omen (vs y-m-n = right/blessing), giving a non-empty, distinctive residue. Falsifiable in principle (a neutral/other sense would refute) but none appears. Caveat: the packet is minimal — a single lexeme in a single construction across all three slots — so universal presence holds trivially with no morphological/constructional diversity to stress-test; not refuted, but the evidence base is narrow.
